'''Mathis Wackernagel''' is a [[Switzerland|Swiss]]-born [[sustainability]] advocate.  He is President of [[Global Footprint Network]], an international sustainability [[think tank]] with offices in [[Oakland]], California, and Geneva, Switzerland. The think-tank is a [[non-profit]] that focuses on developing and promoting [[performance indicator|metrics]] for sustainability.

After earning a degree in [[mechanical engineering]] from the [[ETH Zurich|Swiss Federal Institute of Technology]], he completed his Ph.D. in [[community planning|community]] and [[regional planning]] at the [[University of British Columbia]] in Vancouver, Canada in 1994. There, in his doctoral dissertation under Professor [[William Rees (academic)|William Rees]], he worked with Rees in creating the [[ecological footprint]] concept and developed the accounting methodology for it.<ref>{{Cite thesis |degree=PhD |title=Ecological Footprint and Appropriated Carrying Capacity: A Tool for Planning Toward Sustainability |author=Wackernagel, M. |year=1994 |publisher=School of Community and Regional Planning. The University of British Columbia |location=Vancouver, Canada |url=https://circle.ubc.ca/bitstream/handle/2429/7132/ubc_1994-954027.pdf?sequence=1 |format=PDF |oclc=41839429 |access-date=2011-12-13 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717034651/https://circle.ubc.ca/bitstream/handle/2429/7132/ubc_1994-954027.pdf?sequence=1 |archivedate=2011-07-17 |url-status=dead }}</ref> 
He has worked on sustainability issues for organizations in Europe, Latin America, North America, Asia and Australia.  Wackernagel previously served as the director of the Sustainability Program at Redefining Progress in Oakland, California (1999 - 2003), and directed the Centre for Sustainability Studies / Centro de Estudios para la Sustentabilidad in Mexico (1995-2001). In 2004, he was also adjunct faculty at SAGE of the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]]. In 2010, he was appointed Frank H. T. Rhodes Class of 1956 Visiting Professor at [[Cornell University]] (1 July 2011 – 30 June 2013).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://rhodesprofessors.cornell.edu/RhodesProfsWackernagel.html |title=Mathis Wackernagel Biography |publisher= |access-date=2016-08-09 |archive-date=2016-11-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161108105701/http://rhodesprofessors.cornell.edu/RhodesProfsWackernagel.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2010/04/pillsbury-wackernagel-named-rhodes-professors |title=Pillsbury, Wackernagel named Rhodes professors - Cornell Chronicle |work=www.news.cornell.edu |date=April 2010 |access-date= |archive-date=2016-08-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160809230146/http://www.news.cornell.edu/stories/2010/04/pillsbury-wackernagel-named-rhodes-professors |url-status=live }}</ref> Wackernagel was a member of the [[Global Business Network]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mathis Wackernagel |url=http://www.gbn.com/people/peopledetail.php?id=182 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110913065334/http://www.gbn.com/people/peopledetail.php?id=182 |archive-date=2011-09-13 |website=[[Global Business Network]]}}</ref>

Wackernagel has said that "[[Overshoot (ecology)|Overshoot]] will ultimately liquidate the planet's ecological assets."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.newscientist.com/blog/environment/2007/08/freds-footprint-measuring-our-global_989.html?DCMP=NLC-nletter&nsref=blogenv |title=Measuring our global impact |work=[[New Scientist]] environment blog |date=2007-08-28 |access-date=2 September 2007 |archive-date=2016-02-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160222052925/https://www.newscientist.com/blog/environment/2007/08/freds-footprint-measuring-our-global_989.html?DCMP=NLC-nletter&nsref=blogenv |url-status=live }}</ref> He also noted that "We look at all the problems in separate ways – climate change or biodiversity loss or food shortage – as if they were occurring independently. But they're all symptoms of the same underlying theme: that our collective metabolism, the amount of things that humanity uses, has become very big compared to what Earth can renew."<ref name="DeutscheWelle">{{cite web |url=https://www.dw.com/en/earth-overshoot-day-humans-living-on-ecological-credit/a-65504421 |title=Humans now living on ecological credit |work=[[Deutsche Welle]] Nature and Environment – Global Issues |date=2023-08-02 |access-date=8 August 2023 |archive-date=2023-08-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230808181954/https://www.dw.com/en/earth-overshoot-day-humans-living-on-ecological-credit/a-65504421 |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Università di Siena awarded Mathis Wackernagel with [https://www.unisi.it/unisilife/notizie/mathis-wackernagel-la-laurea-magistrale-ad-honorem-ecotossicologia an honorary degree] on March 21, 2025, for which he provided a "[https://www.unisi.it/unisilife/eventi/laurea-magistrale-ad-honorem-ecotossicologia-mathis-wackernagel lectio magistralis]".

On November 21, 2024, the Nobel Sustainability Trust awarded Wackernagel with the [https://www.nobelsustainabilitytrust.org/the-2024-sustainability-award Award for Leadership in Implementation]. It is the second year the Trust has bestowed this honor; the [https://www.nobelsustainabilitytrust.org/the-sustainability-award-2023 first time] they imparted the implementation award to [[Nicholas Stern, Baron Stern of Brentford|Nicolas Stern]]. 

In November 2022, the University of Stirling [https://twitter.com/stiruni/status/1598293532179038208?s=48&t=6Er2TEp-odeb1CynAv9UDA presented Wackernagel] with an [[Honorary Doctorate|honorary doctorate]]. In his address, [https://www.footprintnetwork.org/2022/11/25/mathis-wackernagel-honorary-degree-university-of-stirling/ he proposed] a "question with which to start everything – whether you design a policy or develop any new strategy [...]: do you love people?"

In 2018, Wackernagel and [https://www.cccep.ac.uk/profile/zhifu-mi/ Zhifu Mi] were the joint recipients of the second ''World Sustainability Award''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mdpi-foundation.org/award/awardees/dr-mathis-wackernagel|title=MDPI Sustainability Foundation|website=wsforum.org|access-date=2019-05-23|archive-date=2023-02-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230201030501/https://mdpi-foundation.org/award/awardees/dr-mathis-wackernagel|url-status=live}}</ref> Wackernagel, along with Susan Burns, received the Skoll Award for Social Entrepreneurship from the [[Skoll Foundation]] in 2007.<ref>{{cite web |title=Global Footprint Network |url=http://skoll.org/organization/global-footprint-network/ |website=skoll.org |access-date=10 April 2020 |archive-date=20 April 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200420233339/https://skoll.org/organization/global-footprint-network/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He received an honorary doctorate from the [[University of Bern]] in 2007, a 2006 [[World Wide Fund for Nature]] Award for Conservation Merit, and the 2005 [[Herman Daly]] Award of the US Society for Ecological Economics.<ref>{{cite web |title=Awards – United States Society for Ecological Economics (USSEE) |url=https://www.ussee.org/about/awards/#.Y7TQjHbMJhE |website=www.ussee.org |access-date=4 April 2024 |language=en |date= |archive-date=9 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240409173026/https://www.ussee.org/about/awards/#.Y7TQjHbMJhE |url-status=live }}</ref> With Global Footprint Network, he received the International Prize [[Calouste Gulbenkian]] 2008 (Lisbon, Portugal) “dedicated to the respect for biodiversity and defense of the environment in man's relationship with nature.”<ref>{{Cite web |title=Apresentação - Fundação Calouste Gulbenkian |trans-title= |url=https://content.gulbenkian.pt/wp-content/uploads/2017/09/28121748/Relatorio2008_00_Apresentacao.pdf |last= |first= |date=2008 |website=Fundação Calouste Gulbenkian |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210123012555/https://content.gulbenkian.pt/wp-content/uploads/2017/09/28121748/Relatorio2008_00_Apresentacao.pdf |archive-date=2021-01-23 |access-date=2020-05-02 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2013, Wackernagel received the ''Prix Nature Swisscanto''.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.natur.ch/index.php?id=963 |title=Natur: Hauptpreis |access-date=2013-03-13 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130507061413/http://www.natur.ch/index.php?id=963 |archivedate=2013-05-07 }}</ref> Prior, he received the ''2012 Binding-Prize for Nature Conservation'',<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.binding.li/html/preisverleihung_2012.html |title=Preisverleihung 2012 |website=www.binding.li |date= |access-date=2024-04-04 |archive-date=2023-09-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230926165733/https://www.binding.li/html/preisverleihung_2012.html |url-status=live }}</ref> the bi-annual Kenneth Boulding Award of the [[International Society for Ecological Economics]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Boulding Award |url=http://www.isecoeco.org/boulding-award/ |website=The International Society for Ecological Economics |date=15 January 2018 |access-date=10 April 2020 |archive-date=3 May 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200503111646/http://www.isecoeco.org/boulding-award/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and the [[Blue Planet Prize]] of the Asahi Glass Foundation (the latter two with [[William E. Rees]]).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.af-info.or.jp/en/blueplanet/list.html |title=Blue Planet Prize : The Laureates - The Asahi Glass Foundation |website=www.af-info.or.jp |date= |access-date=2024-04-04 |archive-date=2016-12-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161225082301/http://af-info.or.jp/en/blueplanet/list.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He also received the ''2011 Zayed International Prize for Environment'' <ref name="Data Sources">{{cite web |url=https://www.zayedprize.org.ae/fifth-cycle#tab-4 |title=Zayed International Prize for the Environment |website=www.zayedprize.org.ae |date= |access-date=2024-04-04 |archive-date=2024-03-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240329050328/https://www.zayedprize.org.ae/fifth-cycle#tab-4 |url-status=live }}</ref> in the category "action leading to positive change in society."  The Zayed prize recognized Wackernagel's contribution to “translate[ing] the complexity of humanity's impact on the environment and natural resources into a more understandable and actionable form. The concept of ‘ecological limits' and relating the demands of human beings to the planet's available ecological resources, has attracted and is catalyzing action among governments, business and civil society."

The (En)Rich List ranked Wackernagel as the 19th of the 100 most inspirational individuals whose contributions enrich paths to sustainable futures.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://enrichlist.org/the-list/mathis-wackernagel/ | title=Mathis Wackernagel | website=enrichlist.org | date=7 March 2012 | access-date= | archive-date=27 June 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170627124617/http://enrichlist.org/the-list/mathis-wackernagel/ | url-status=live }}</ref>
